topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning objectives on cancer causation, and sets expectations for understanding environmental and genetic carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Genetic and Endogenous Foundations of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish that cancer is a genetic and evolutionary disease arising from somatic mutations, endogenous cellular metabolic processes, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence in Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine external carcinogenic exposures, the ongoing debate between environmental causation and mutational bad luck, and epidemiological patterns of global cancer incidence.

topics.label: Oncogenic Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how infectious pathogens promote cancer development, focusing on Epstein-Barr virus and malaria in the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Xenobiotic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation, dietary toxins, and chemical agents undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Host Susceptibility, and Mechanistic Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic tumor promoters, the multi-stage model of carcinogenesis, host developmental timing, and summarize the key mechanisms of cancer causation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogens and Mutational Signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and measure mutagenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by synthesizing the balance between environmental risks, lifestyle choices, and practical decision-making.
